tree.approach: ANSWERED. Work in the periodic Maya-diagram (bead) model. TWO DELIVERABLES BEYOND THE PAPER. (1) The paper says 'by induction on the (finite) number of steps' and never names the terminating measure; Lean will not accept that. The measure is `RobinHood.gap l sigma nu = sum_{r<l} (psum nu r - psum sigma r)`, the area between the two partial-sum profiles: >= 0 iff sigma <| nu (`gap_nonneg`), and a Robin Hood step drops it strictly because the profile falls by one on the window (a,b] and r=b is in range (`gap_lt`). The induction is on (gap l sigma nu).toNat. This confirms the measure conjectured in the 2026-09-22 c2 LEAN brief. (2) The side condition b < l is NOT a conclusion of `robin_hood_step` and had to be recovered from the size equation psum (ex a b nu) l = psum nu l (`exch_snd_lt`): a < l because nu a >= nu b + 2 >= 2 > 0, and then the size equation forces b < l. The paper never states this and the gap measure is undefined without it.
SHARPENING: the size and non-negativity conditions on W itself (every beta in W has sum beta = d and beta >= 0), which the brief listed as hypothesis (hsum), are NOT consumed -- the needed instances are carried by IsPart and by the theorem's own psum sigma l = psum nu l. SORTING BRIDGE: the paper's appeal to S_l-stability plus sorting collapses to a single pointwise identity, `ex a (a+1) (nu o swap (a+1) b) = (ex a b nu) o swap (a+1) b` -- the near exchange on the twisted vector IS the far exchange, twisted; swap is an involution, so one more hperm untwists it.
CONTROLS. `hyps_satisfiable`: W = univ satisfies hperm and hexch, so the hypotheses are not contradictory (weak -- the conclusion is free). `hexch_load_bearing`: the S_2-orbit W_0 = {(3,1),(1,3)} satisfies EVERY hypothesis except hexch, with nu = (3,1) in W_0, sigma = (2,2) a partition of 4 with sigma <| nu, and sigma NOT in W_0. The BROWSE addendum to the brief proposed Q198 (the converse of Naprienko 2301.12110 Lemma 4.4) as the opening move, on the reading that a ribbon's one-bead hop k -> K+1 is the shape of an M-convexity exchange. It is not the move this problem needs. A RIBBON of size r is one bead hopping r sites, jumping freely over occupied sites; a HORIZONTAL STRIP of size r is several beads hopping right with pairwise DISJOINT closed trajectories (Lemma 2.6). Cylindric skew Schur functions are built from horizontal strips, so the ribbon move is the wrong local move. The move that actually implements the exchange axiom is smaller: one bead in one row of the chain slides ONE site.

children.approach: Prop 8.3 (prop:minimal), NEW 2026-09-25 c2: any convex, S_l-stable K subset R^l containing the partition lambdahat contains every alpha in N^l with sort(alpha) <| lambdahat; hence P_lambdahat, the smallest such K, does. Proof: reduce to partitions by S_l-stability; iterate the Robin Hood step DOWNWARD from lambdahat to sigma; each step lands on the segment [nu, (a b)nu] by `segment-step`, and (a b)nu is in K by S_l-stability, so convexity carries the induction. THIS IS A RE-PROOF OF RADO's DIRECTION (equivalently Hardy-Littlewood-Polya majorisation), by the CLASSICAL argument -- lem:hlp is the classical transfer/Muirhead step. NO NOVELTY IS CLAIMED. What is new is only that the engine was already in the paper, proved for an unrelated purpose (prop:ideal), so the paper CITES nothing. The three failure modes an argument of this shape is prone to were each checked rather than assumed: (1) does t = 1/g lie in [0,1]? yes, g >= 2 from lem:hlp, and `segment-step` needs only g >= 1; (2) does the induction terminate? yes, Phi(t) = sum_{r=1}^{l} (N_r - S_r) is a non-negative integer dropping by exactly b_t - a_t >= 1 per step -- this is the decreasing statistic the route needed and did not have; (3) does it terminate at PERMUTATIONS of lambdahat, or only at points of J? This is where a short HLP-type proof usually leaks, and it is avoided by inducting on MEMBERSHIP in K rather than tracking coefficients. Checked constructively anyway: the induction was UNROLLED into an explicit rational convex combination and every support point required to be a genuine permutation of lambdahat. 725 pairs (lambdahat,sigma) with sigma <| lambdahat, |sigma| <= 9, l <= 4; 1174 Robin Hood steps, every one with gap >= 2 and Phi strictly decreasing; coefficients non-negative summing to exactly 1; combination equal to sigma exactly; 0 failures. Also side-condition b_t <= l proved (sigma has at most l parts, so sigma_j > 0 forces j <= l), without which the chain leaves R^l. Code proofs/code-q261/rado_from_robin_hood.py (V2).

Lem 8.2 (lem:segment), NEW 2026-09-25 c2: for nu in R^l and a != b with g = nu_a - nu_b >= 1, one has nu - e_a + e_b = (1-1/g) nu + (1/g) (a b).nu, a convex combination. One line of algebra: tau - nu = g(e_b - e_a). HYPOTHESIS AUDIT (which line breaks if I drop it): the Robin Hood step supplies g >= 2, but this lemma needs only g >= 1 -- at g = 1 the combination degenerates to nu - e_a + e_b = (a b).nu, which is correct. So the stronger inequality nu_a >= nu_b + 2 is NOT consumed downstream; it is needed only inside the proof of the Robin Hood step itself, to make tau a partition STRICTLY below nu. Stated at g >= 1 deliberately, so that a hypothesis of the engine does not masquerade as a constraint on the object.

Rick's Remark A, now MINE: DERIVED and verified, not inherited. Two statements. (1) Closed form: unrolling the greedy recursion g^t_i = min(g^{t-1}_{i+1} - 1, lambda_i) gives g^t_i = min(min_{0<=s<t}(lambda_{i+s} - s), mu_{i+t} - t), and the inner minimum is attained at s = 0 because lambda is STRICTLY INCREASING, so lambda_{i+s} >= lambda_i + s. Hence g^t_i = min(lambda_i, mu_{i+t} - t). THE BRIEF FLAGGED THE DIRECTION OF THIS INEQUALITY AND IT IS THE RIGHT WAY ROUND: rows are indexed downward and bead positions increase, so lambda_{i+1} >= lambda_i + 1 is exactly what the bead model gives. Checked rather than assumed. (2) Finiteness with an EXPLICIT bound, which Rick did not give: mu_{i+km} - km = mu_i + k(n-m) and n > m, so l_min <= k*m with k = max_i ceil((lambda_i - mu_i)/(n-m)). Hence l_min < infinity for EVERY mu subset lambda. CONSEQUENCE, which is the valuable part: the l_min = infinity branch of the Stabilisation lemma of note 3 and its trailing clause are VACUOUS, and the main theorem of note 3 did not need its F_w != 0 detour. Both deleted, and the deletion is recorded in rem:deadbranch rather than done silently -- a vacuous branch is a case distinction nobody checks. Written up as a numbered lemma with proof (lem:lminfinite) in note 3. VERIFIED at first hand: the closed form (both the two-term form and the full-min form) checked against the recursion for t <= 40, the absorption inequality lambda_{i+s} - s >= lambda_i checked directly, l_min finite and <= k*m checked, over 3032 shapes with n <= 7 and d <= 9, 0 failures. Code proofs/code-q261/remarks_A_B.py. Promoted peer-claimed -> proved on MY derivation; Rick's 5,947,200 (t,i)-checks are corroboration, not the warrant.

Rick's Remark B: gamma = (u(g^t) - u(g^{t-1}))_t is already weakly decreasing, so gamma = lambdahat and the sort can be dropped THERE. NOT PROMOTED TO `proved`, deliberately: I verified it (3032 shapes, n <= 7, d <= 9, 0 failures, remarks_A_B.py) but I did NOT derive it. The natural route does not close: by the closed form of `rick-remark-A-greedy-closed-form`, u(g^t) = sum_i min(lambda_i, mu_{i+t} - t), and weak decrease of gamma is CONCAVITY of t |-> u(g^t); but t |-> mu_{i+t} - t need not be concave termwise, since the gaps mu_{i+t+1} - mu_{i+t} of a cylindric shape are not monotone in t. So if it is true it is true of the SUM over i, not term by term, and I have not found the argument. `computed` is the honest grade. It removes the sort from gamma, the greedy chain's OWN weight -- a special element. The unformalised bridge is `sorted-form-equals-subset-form`, which is about an ARBITRARY alpha, where the sort does real work. Different object. A true statement about a special element read as a statement about all of them.
